hints: Focus on working out which hydrocarbon is saturated and which is unsaturated by drawing out $R-CH_3$ and $R'-CH_3$ fully.
Remember that $R$ contains a $C=C$ double bond, so $R'-CH_3$ is the saturated alkane that needs a propagation step.
Recall that propagation keeps radicals going ($radical + molecule \rightarrow new radical$), while termination removes radicals ($radical + radical \rightarrow molecule$).
walkthrough:
**Identify the saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons**

Think like a detective and build the full molecules. $R$ is $CH_3CHC(CH_3)$, so $R-CH_3$ is $CH_3-CH=C(CH_3)-CH_3$.

This is 2-methylbut-2-ene, an alkene, so it is unsaturated.

**Check the other hydrocarbon**

$R'$ is $CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_2$, so $R'-CH_3$ is $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$.

This is 2-methylbutane, an alkane with only single bonds, so it is saturated.

**Recall propagation vs termination**

Propagation has one radical on each side and keeps the chain going:
$$RH + Br\bullet \rightarrow R\bullet + HBr$$
$$R\bullet + Br_2 \rightarrow RBr + Br\bullet$$

**Apply to the correct row**

Termination joins two radicals to make a stable molecule with no radicals:
$$R\bullet + R\bullet \rightarrow R-R$$
$$R\bullet + Br\bullet \rightarrow RBr$$
So we need propagation using $R'$ and termination using $R$, which matches only one row.

options.A: Both equations show $radical + radical \rightarrow molecule$, which is termination, not propagation. The left side also wrongly uses $R$, the unsaturated hydrocarbon, for the saturated case.
options.B: The left equation $R-CH_2\bullet + Br_2 \rightarrow R-CH_2Br + Br\bullet$ is propagation but uses $R$ (unsaturated) instead of $R'$ (saturated). The right equation is also propagation, not termination, and uses the wrong hydrocarbon.
options.C: Left side $R'-CH_3 + Br\bullet \rightarrow R'-CH_2\bullet + HBr$ is the first propagation step for the saturated alkane. Right side $2R-CH_2\bullet \rightarrow R-CH_2CH_2-R$ joins two radicals with no radicals left, so it is termination for the unsaturated hydrocarbon.
options.D: The two types are swapped. $2R'-CH_2\bullet \rightarrow R'-CH_2CH_2-R'$ is termination, not propagation, and $R-CH_3 + Br\bullet \rightarrow R-CH_2\bullet + HBr$ is propagation, not termination.
